one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-08) almost certainly contains Corning's Q3 2026 report (not yet confirmed; Q3 2025 was reported on Oct 28, so late October is expected) against guidance of core sales $4.9-5.0B and core EPS $0.85-0.89 [1], plus hyperscaler Q3 reports with 2027 capex commentary and Fujikura/Prysmian Q3 updates. Value-chain reads into the print are positive: Amphenol book-to-bill 1.23 [10], Lumentum guiding +~24% q/q and reportedly capacity committed into 2029 [9,12], fibre makers' profits multiplying on tight preform supply [5,8,11]. But the last print shows the asymmetry: a beat with a guide only in line sent the stock down ~19% on the day [14], and the stock has realized ~60% annualized vol over the past year [4]. With no strong directional edge, I centre the distribution at today's price with a widened 1-month sigma (~19% log, i.e. annual vol/3.5 plus an earnings bump), a very slight upward drift from the peer read-through offset by the July precedent.

fair_value.method: Blend of (a) 30x (peer median 29.5x) on Oct-2027 NTM EPS of ~$5.19 = $156 and (b) a Springboard cross-check: $30B end-2028 run-rate x 16.6% net margin / 875M shares = $5.69 x 30x = $171, discounted 1.17 years at 10% = $153. Weighted 70/30 = ~$155.

inputs_detail.derivation: 4.37 x 1.25. Springboard targets a 19% sales CAGR Q4'26-Q4'30 [1]; consensus has FY2027 EPS growing 33% on 19.6% revenue growth [3], i.e. ~13pts of leverage; I assume about half that leverage (~6pts) in 2028, so EPS +25%.

Peer median forward P/E 29.5x (range 17.5x-50.7x, 12 peers). GLW trades at 42.3x [2] but its FY2027 EPS growth (33%) is slightly below the peer median next-year growth (~36%), it is more capital-intensive and has a large flat Glass/Auto base, so no persistent premium is justified; 30x is at the median.

Cost of equity for a beta-1.12 [2] large cap; equity-risk judgment, discounting $171 over 1.17 years: 171/1.10^1.17 = 153.

bear.story: AI optical spend digests in 2027 while competitors restart idle preform capacity [5] and fibre makers flush with record profits [7,8,11] add supply, fibre prices that rose 80%+ in China [5] normalize, Meta-type contracts run at the low end of 'up to' [6]; FY2028 EPS ~$4.6 and the multiple de-rates to ~20x as growth falls toward the TEL/PRY end of the peer set.

base.story: Springboard stays on track ($20B run-rate end-2026, heading for $30B end-2028 [1]), Optical keeps growing 25-30% on enterprise/hyperscale fibre while Glass/Auto stay flat; EPS compounds ~25-30% but the multiple converges from 42x toward the ~30x peer median, so the stock roughly tracks fair value.

bull.story: Fibre tightness persists through 2027 (preform is the bottleneck [5]; Lumentum and Amphenol signal multi-year AI backlog [9,10,12]), Corning beats Springboard and lifts 2028 targets, FY2028 EPS above $6 and the market keeps paying high-30s multiples as it did in June (record $271 [14]).

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: We use 30x forward P/E, at the peer median 29.5x. GLW trades at 42.3x forward and 34.7x trailing EV/EBITDA [2], above the median on P/E and roughly at the median on trailing EV/EBITDA.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium applied. GLW's FY2027 consensus EPS growth (+33% [3]) is in line with or below the peer median (~36%); roughly 47% of Q2 core sales (Glass Innovations, Automotive, Life Sciences) grew -15% to +2% in Q2 [1]; and fibre is a capacity-cyclical commodity-like product where competitors are adding capacity aggressively. The Meta contract [6] and Springboard targets [1] give visibility but not structurally higher returns than peers like APH. A discount was not applied either, because Optical (44% of Q2 sales, +32% [1]) has the same AI exposure as the peer set.

thesis_break_reason: $100 is ~23x consensus FY2027 EPS [3] and below the July post-earnings panic low (~$114.5 intraday [4]). Trading there would most likely mean the market believes the AI fibre demand/pricing cycle has turned (hyperscaler capex cut, fibre price collapse as competitor capacity arrives) or Springboard's $30B 2028 target is being withdrawn, rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise.

reasoning: Lane: industry/value chain. Facts from the Q2 8-K [1]: core sales $4.74B (+17%), core EPS $0.78 (+30%), Optical $2.07B (+32%, enterprise +65%), Glass Innovations +1%, Auto +2%, Life Sciences -15%; Q3 guide $0.85-0.89; Springboard $20B/$30B/$40B run-rates for 2026/2028/2030; net debt ~$5.9B. The chain strongly confirms demand: CRU reports Chinese fibre prices +80% Nov-25 to Jan-26 with preform the bottleneck [5]; YOFC H1 profit +711-914% [11]; Fujikura Q1 sales +50%, OP +155% and raised FY guidance [8]; Prysmian Digital Solutions +18% organic with margin 23.8% [7]; Amphenol (owner of competitor CommScope) +30% organic, book-to-bill 1.23 [10]; Lumentum +109% y/y with Q1 guide $1.25B midpoint [9] and reportedly capacity committed to early 2029 [12]. The flip side, also from the chain: every major fibre maker is adding capacity, and Corning's share of the spoils is shared with Fujikura, Prysmian, CommScope/Amphenol and Chinese makers; Bernstein initiated GLW at Market Perform while rating optical component peers Outperform [13]. Valuation: at 42.3x forward [2] GLW is above a 12-name AI-infrastructure peer median of 29.5x while its next-year growth (+33%) is at or below the peer median (~36%), so I apply ~30x to Oct-2027 NTM EPS (~$5.19) => ~$156, cross-checked by a Springboard run-rate method (~$153): fair value ~$155, about today's price. Consensus target $188 [3] is noted but not used. Distribution: median ~$155, roughly lognormal with ~50% annual sigma (below the ~60% realized [4], which was inflated by the June spike to $271 and the July -46% month [14]), with fat tails both ways from the AI cycle; bear $95 (25%), base $160 (50%), bull $235 (25%). Research limits: Twelve Data statistics/estimates endpoints were plan-restricted; hyperscaler capex figures found in search could not be opened at source and were left out of the valuation; peer EV/EBITDA is trailing only.
